actions.name: Join or start a room
actions.summary: Opens a conversation on a content topic over encrypted transport. Starting and joining are the same call: the instance opens the topic holding a fresh epoch key that only it has. It reads nothing already in the room until an existing member admits it (room/admit-member). Nothing is agreed, so there is no agreement field.

requirements.name: delivery_module
requirements.target: delivery_module

requirements.name: delivery-node
requirements.target: the delivery createNode config in Settings (default: the logos.test fleet's entry nodes)

requirements.name: encryption-identity
requirements.target: the keystore's Ed25519/X25519 identity (F-14)

steps.who: the member joining or starting the room
steps.does: Normalizes the room name to a 4-segment Waku content topic, /muster/1/<name>/proto (an already valid topic passes through), so two peers who name the same room derive the same topic. If the instance already has a session on that topic it re-activates it. Otherwise it opens a CoordinationSession over the delivery transport with a fresh EpochCrypto: epoch 0, a new random key, members = this instance only. Joining also clears any stored invite to that topic. It then announces the room's join key on the topic (a beacon): 32 bytes derived from its current epoch key, naming no member, so someone who knows only the topic can ask to join without saying who they are in the clear.

Subscribes to the topic and polls the store every ~1 s (MUSTER_CATCHUP_MS, floor 200 ms) for a 60 s window (MUSTER_CATCHUP_LOOKBACK_MS), round-robin across the configured entry nodes; the first ticks per topic fetch deeper history. It ingests only envelopes it can open: it tries each epoch key it holds, newest first, and the one whose MAC verifies is the envelope's epoch. An envelope sealed under an epoch it holds no key for is skipped. No epoch number rides outside the seal, so a store node sees the same shape in every epoch.

steps.who: every instance holding the same events
steps.does: Reduces the log to state. Two instances that hold the same event set reach the same state digest, whatever the delivery order or duplication; a member who comes online late catches up from the store.

refusals.what: opening an envelope sealed under an epoch this instance was never granted
refusals.why: it holds no key for that epoch; the envelope is skipped, never guessed (F-16, invariant 7)

actions.ui: Composer.qml → Main.qml enterRoom (a new room); Home.qml room list and the Room.qml topic field (an existing room)

claims.claim: An envelope from an epoch this instance holds no key for is never opened.
Instances holding the same events reach the same state, in any order.

The store node sees the room's topic in the clear, when this instance publishes and polls, each frame's size and kind, and the room's join key. It sees no member identity and no epoch number (store_node_view_test).

The composer names a new room with random bits only (muster.room.<16 hex>): not the activity, not the peer, not the time. What the room is for and who it is with travel inside the sealed invite and the room.
Home's titles for rooms this instance opened or was invited to live only in this session; after a restart the list shows each room's topic.

evidence.what: musterCoordinateJoin + toContentTopic: topic normalization, one fresh epoch per session
the store catch-up period, window and store-peer rotation
derivedTopic: muster.room.<16 random hex> — no verb, no peer, no time (exo-661.7)

actions.name: Ask to join a room, and admit a member
actions.summary: The membership handshake. A joiner sends a signed binding of its encryption identity, sealed to the room's announced join key so only members can read it; any existing member decides whether to admit it. Admission re-keys the room forward: the joiner gets the new epoch's key and nothing earlier (F-16). One member decides; nothing is agreed, so there is no agreement field.

requirements.name: identity-binding
requirements.target: the joiner's secp256k1 key vouching for its Ed25519/X25519 identity (F-9, F-14)

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

steps.who: the joiner (it has joined the topic but holds no key the room uses)
steps.does: coordinate_request_join sends the joiner's binding: its encryption identity (Ed25519 ‖ X25519, 64 bytes) and a context {account: the room topic, slot: "0", expiry: now + 1 day}, signed by the joiner's secp256k1 key. It travels sealed (a libsodium sealed box) to each join key the room has announced on the topic, one join-request frame (kind 0x01) per key, at most 8. A join key is derived from an epoch key, so only a member holding that epoch can open the request. With no join key seen yet the joiner pulls the store's retained frames; if there is still none it publishes a beacon request (kind 0x05, a random nonce) that members answer with their current join key (kind 0x04), and the call returns "waiting-for-room-key", which the scope panel shows until the ask is sent. The UI re-sends every 3 s, up to 20 times, until the roster grows, because a single send can miss every store node on a sparse shard. A request carries no authority.
steps.signs: secp256k1 recoverable signature over digest(hash-input "muster.identity-binding.v1" {ed25519, x25519, account, slot, expiry})

steps.does: coordinate_pending opens each request with the join keys this member holds and lists those not yet admitted: each identity, its contact alias, and bindsOwner — whether the binding's recovered signer is a signer of an account disclosed in the room (F-9). The member decides. Admission is not gated on owning anything.

coordinate_admit(identity) requires a pending binding for that identity that recovers a signer and has not expired. It then re-keys forward: a new epoch, a fresh random key, members = the old roster plus the joiner. For every member of the new epoch it publishes a control frame (kind 0x02): the epoch number, every member's 64-byte identity and the new key, all sealed together to that member's X25519 key in a libsodium sealed box, so the topic carries one anonymous box per member and no roster. It then publishes membership/<epoch>/admit/<joiner> into the log, sealed under the new epoch, and announces the new epoch's join key. When the room was started by naming a person, Room.qml admits that identity as soon as its request arrives; the module still checks the binding.
steps.signs: nothing is signed. The grants are sealed boxes. The membership event names the joiner and no author, so the room cannot tell which member admitted.

steps.who: the joiner, and every existing member
steps.does: Each tries every grant; only the one sealed to its own X25519 key opens. The joiner learns the new epoch's number, key and member list, then reads every envelope sealed at that epoch or later, starting with its own admission. Nothing sealed earlier opens for it. Existing members move to the new epoch too.

refusals.why: a request admits nobody and grants no key; a member has to decide

refusals.what: admitting an identity whose binding has expired or does not recover a signer
refusals.why: coordinate_admit returns "unverified"; bindingSigner raises on an expired binding (F-9)

refusals.what: admitting an identity that is not 64 bytes (Ed25519 ‖ X25519)
refusals.why: coordinate_admit returns "bad-key"

refusals.what: the joiner reading anything sealed before its admission
refusals.why: it is granted only the new epoch's key; earlier keys are disjoint (F-16, invariant 7)

refusals.what: a member opening a grant wrapped to someone else
refusals.why: a sealed box opens only for its recipient

actions.ui: ScopePanel.qml in Room.qml (Ask to join · pending requests · Admit); Room.qml auto-admits the peer named in Composer.qml

claims.claim: A joiner reads from its own admission on, and nothing sealed before it.
A join request grants nothing until a member admits it.
Any member can admit anyone whose binding is valid; who gets in rests on each member's judgement.

The store node sees that someone asked to join and when, and at every admit how many members received the new key (one grant each), so the room's size. It sees no identity, no address, no roster and no epoch number (store_node_view_test).
The admit event names the joiner, not the member who admitted them.
No hosted method removes a member. The epoch layer supports removal, but nothing calls it, so an admitted member reads every later epoch.

Anyone on the topic can announce a join key of their own; a joiner who knows the room only by name seals a copy of its request to every join key it has seen, so whoever announced a false one learns who is asking. The store node's passive view is unaffected; an invite names the inviter, but the join still follows the topic's announced keys.
claims.party: anyone who publishes on the room's topic

evidence.what: frame kinds: a join request (0x01) is sealed to an announced join key (0x04, answered on a beacon request 0x05); a grant (0x02) is sealed whole to one member
admit: epoch ‖ member count ‖ every identity ‖ key, sealed to each member; envelopes carry no epoch header; join keys derived from epoch keys
encodeLink: the binding travels as identity ‖ context ‖ signature
the live two-instance handshake over the Logos fleet

actions.name: Re-announce open proposals to a new member
actions.summary: After an admit, re-seals every open proposal into the current epoch so the new member can see and act on it. Approvals made before it arrived are not re-shared: they stay in their epoch. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

steps.who: a member, right after an admit (Room.qml calls it after every Admit)
steps.does: For each intent that is not submitted, settling or final, coordinate_reannounce re-publishes into the current epoch: its policy declaration, its propose event (the effect), its signing context and recorded reads, and a new intent-ref message {kind: intent-ref, intentId}. The events are content-addressed, so re-publishing yields the same ids and members who hold them fold nothing new. Returns {reannounced: count}.
steps.signs: Only the intent-ref message is signed, with the re-announcer's author signature. Ed25519, by the author's encryption identity (its signing half, F-14), over digest(hash-input "muster.event.author.v1" {room: the content topic, key: the event key, parents: sorted, author: the author's 64-byte identity hex, value: the event value as dCBOR without authorSig}). The signature is added to the value as authorSig (exo-f76).

steps.does: Folds the re-announced intents and sees their cards. It holds the context and reads, so it can attest its own approval. Approvals made before its epoch are not in its log.

refusals.what: re-announcing an intent that is submitted, settling or final
refusals.why: finished intents are skipped

refusals.what: handing the new member approvals made before its epoch
refusals.why: approvals are not re-published; what members signed before the joiner arrived stays in its epoch (F-16)

actions.ui: Room.qml, after every Admit (ScopePanel.qml or the auto-admit); no button of its own

claims.claim: A member admitted after a proposal can see and approve it without reading anything from before its epoch.
Approvals made before the new member's epoch stay unreadable to it.
A new member sees open proposals only if some member re-announces them; the UI does so after every admit, a headless host must call it itself.

evidence.what: liveReannounce: what is re-published, what is skipped
reannounce() after every admit

actions.name: Invite someone to a room
actions.summary: Drops a sealed invite on a peer's inbox topic, so they learn the room's topic without any prior contact. Only the named peer can open it; it grants nothing — they still have to be admitted. The room topic, the note and the inviter's claimed chat id reach only the recipient, a party the observer vocabulary has no class for. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: peer-chat-id
requirements.target: the peer's 64-byte encryption identity (Ed25519 ‖ X25519)

requirements.name: delivery_module
requirements.target: delivery_module

steps.does: coordinate_invite(peer chat id, room topic, note) builds {topic, from: the inviter's chat id, note, ts}, seals it to the peer's X25519 key in a libsodium sealed box, and publishes it as an invite frame (kind 0x03) on the peer's inbox topic: /muster/1/muster.inbox.<hex>/proto, where hex is the first 8 bytes of sha256("muster-inbox-v1" ‖ the peer's chat id hex). The store retains it, so the peer need not be online. Main.qml sends one when the composer names a person by chat id.
steps.signs: nothing. A sealed box encrypts but does not authenticate the sender: 'from' is the inviter's claim.

steps.does: coordinate_start_inbox subscribes to its own inbox topic and pulls what the store kept. The UI calls it at launch, and coordinate_invites starts it too if it isn't running (the launch call can land before the module answers and be lost), so Home's 2 s poll always brings the inbox up. coordinate_invites opens each frame with the keystore; frames that do not open or parse are skipped. It dedups by (from, topic) and hides invites for rooms already joined, invites the user dismissed (kept in dismissed_invites.json beside the keystore) and, when MUSTER_INVITES_SINCE is set, older ones.
Joins the room (room/join), then asks to be admitted (room/admit-member), or dismisses the invite (coordinate_dismiss_invite: local, persisted, nothing is sent).

refusals.what: a peer chat id that is not 64 bytes
refusals.why: coordinate_invite returns {error: bad peer chat id}

refusals.what: anyone but the named recipient opening the invite
refusals.why: a sealed box opens only for the X25519 key it was sealed to

refusals.what: an invite letting the recipient read the room
refusals.why: it names a topic and grants no key; a member must still admit the recipient

actions.ui: Composer.qml (people step) → Main.qml sendInvite; Home.qml shows received invites (Join · Dismiss)

claims.claim: Only the named recipient can open an invite.
An invite grants nothing; the recipient must still be admitted.
Anyone who knows a chat id can compute its inbox topic and watch invite traffic to it — count and timing, never contents.
The inviter named in an invite is the sender's claim: a sealed box does not authenticate its sender.
An invite waits in the store until the recipient's inbox fetches it: an inbox that starts later still receives it (invite-proof.sh fetched an invite sent during an earlier run).

sendInvite: the invite frame is published without epoch sealing

actions.name: Post a chat message or card
actions.summary: Posts a chat line, or a typed card (address-request, address-share, receipt, fact, intent-ref) as JSON, into the room's sealed log. The author signs it; the room drops a message whose author did not sign it (exo-f76). Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

steps.does: coordinate_post_message(body) builds message/<id> with value {author: its encryption identity hex, ts: unix seconds, body}. The core never interprets body. id is the first 12 bytes of keccak256(author ‖ body ‖ ts as 8 little-endian bytes ‖ a per-instance counter as 8 little-endian bytes). The author signs; the event is sealed to the current epoch and published. Returns the id.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by the author's encryption identity (its signing half, F-14), over digest(hash-input "muster.event.author.v1" {room: the content topic, key: the event key, parents: sorted, author: the author's 64-byte identity hex, value: the event value as dCBOR without authorSig}). The signature is added to the value as authorSig (exo-f76).

steps.does: Opens the envelope and keeps the event in its log. The room's views read the authentic log: a message whose authorSig does not verify for the author it names, in this room, is dropped from every view but stays in the raw log. Messages fold oldest-first; JSON cards render through MusterCard.qml.

refusals.why: authenticEvents drops it; every view reads only the authentic log (invariant 9)

refusals.what: signing a message in another member's name
refusals.why: signAuthored refuses an event that names anyone but the keystore's own identity

refusals.what: a genuine message replayed into another room
refusals.why: the signature binds the room topic

refusals.what: an edited body or re-parented message
refusals.why: the signature binds the value and the parents

refusals.what: a malformed signature or value
refusals.why: rejected without raising (exo-cf7)

actions.name: Decline a proposal (Deny)
actions.summary: The card's Deny. Publishes a signed decline so the room sees who is out. It is informational: the driver's threshold and the lifecycle are untouched. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

The signature is added to the value as authorSig (exo-f76).

actions.name: Share an address or holding into a proposal
actions.summary: Fills a slot a proposal asks of you — a payee's receiving address, say — with one of your own holdings (exo-45e K5). Only its public face, class and form travel, bound to the proposal and the effect field it fills; the sharer signs it. The hosted catalogue holds only EVM material today: your secp keys, an EVM receive address per key, the Safes disclosed in the room, and ETH. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: the slot the proposal asks of you
requirements.target: the chain the proposal's requirement names

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

disclosure.field: the shared public face (the effect field it fills)
the shared field, if the proposal's driver discloses it

steps.who: the member asked for material (a contributor or counterparty)
steps.does: coordinate_offers(intentId) crosses the proposal's manifest requirements with this instance's own catalogue. For each slot it returns candidates as public faces with their F-10 grade and the disclosure rows choosing them would add. It reads only this instance's holdings; it never names another member's.

coordinate_share_material(intentId, requirement, public) requires the requirement to exist and name an effect field, and the public face to be one of this instance's holdings of that class. It publishes intent/<id>/material/<requirement>/<its identity> with {public, form, class, field} and its author signature. The handle never leaves the instance.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by the author's encryption identity (its signing half, F-14), over digest(hash-input "muster.event.author.v1" {room: the content topic, key: the event key, parents: sorted, author: the author's 64-byte identity hex, value: the event value as dCBOR without authorSig}). The signature is added to the value as authorSig (exo-f76).

actions.name: Disclose an account into the room
actions.summary: Makes an account exist to the room: a Safe, a Bitcoin multisig or a LEZ multisig. The discloser signs it; every reader checks it against the chain itself. Account-bound policies (safe, eip191, the Bitcoin and LEZ kinds) act only from a disclosed account. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: account
requirements.target: a CAIP-10 account on a CAIP-2 chain

requirements.name: rpc
requirements.target: the chain's RPC in Settings (rpc for EVM, lez-rpc for a LEZ multisig; none for Bitcoin)

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

steps.does: coordinate_disclose_account({family, chain, address, label, signers?, threshold?, config?}). evm.safe: omitted signers or threshold are read from the chain through the RPC, and the disclosure is refused if they cannot be; a threshold above the signer count is refused. Bitcoin (btc.p2wsh-sortedmulti, btc.tapscript-multi-a): signers (33-byte keys) and threshold are required, the address is derived from them, and a given address must match; no chain read. lez.multisig-program: config {program, createKey, pda, layout}; the address must be the state PDA the config derives; members and threshold are read from the chain and a disagreement is refused. It then publishes account/<CAIP-10>/disclose/<its identity> with the account and its author signature.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by the author's encryption identity (its signing half, F-14), over digest(hash-input "muster.event.author.v1" {room: the content topic, key: the event key, parents: sorted, author: the author's 64-byte identity hex, value: the event value as dCBOR without authorSig}). The signature is added to the value as authorSig (exo-f76).

steps.does: coordinate_accounts folds one account per CAIP-10 id, naming every discloser. If members disclosed different signers or thresholds, conflict is set and the first in canonical order governs. Each reader checks the disclosure itself: an EVM account through its own RPC, a Bitcoin account by re-deriving the address, a LEZ multisig by reading the PDA. The result is verified, disagrees (naming what differs) or unknown, never a false verified. For a Safe it also reads the enabled modules and guard — the ways around the threshold — and reports unknown when unread.

refusals.what: a LEZ multisig whose address is not the PDA its config derives

actions.name: Run a FROST key ceremony in the room
actions.summary: ChillDKG with the room as its coordinator: members open a t-of-n ceremony, the first n to join are the participants, and each computes its steps from the log. The result is a t-of-n account (btc.frost-bip445, or a LEZ FROST account on a lez: network) disclosed into the room with its public recovery data. No share or nonce enters the log. Spending from the account is a family action.

agreement.threshold: all n participants (the first n members to join) must complete both steps
agreement.finality: in-room: done when each participant has finalized and disclosed the account
agreement.domain: ChillDKG (bip-chilldkg draft) with a host key per ceremony

requirements.name: frost-host-key
requirements.target: a host key the keystore derives under the label frost/<ceremony id>

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

disclosure.field: step messages (commitments, encrypted shares, certifying signatures)

steps.does: frost_ceremony_open(id, network, t, n) requires 1 ≤ t ≤ n, n ≥ 2 and an id without '/'. It publishes frost/<id>/open {network, t, n} (network defaults to regtest; a lez: network yields a LEZ account) and joins.
steps.signs: nothing. The open event names no author, so the room cannot tell who opened the ceremony.

steps.does: frost_ceremony_join(id): the keystore derives a host key for this ceremony (never exported) and the member publishes frost/<id>/join/<its identity> {host: the 33-byte host public key} with its author signature. The first n joins in canonical order are the participants.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by the author's encryption identity (its signing half, F-14), over digest(hash-input "muster.event.author.v1" {room: the content topic, key: the event key, parents: sorted, author: the author's 64-byte identity hex, value: the event value as dCBOR without authorSig}). The signature is added to the value as authorSig (exo-f76).

steps.who: each participant, on its client's coordinate_intents tick (at most every 2 s)
steps.does: Step 1: publishes frost/<id>/pmsg1/<host>: its VSS commitment, proof of possession, and shares encrypted to each participant's host key. Every member computes the coordinator's step from the log. Step 2: publishes frost/<id>/pmsg2/<host>, its CertEq certifying signature. Finalize: its keystore checks the certificate, and the participant discloses the t-of-n account (account/<CAIP-10>/disclose/<its identity>) with config {ceremony, recovery}.
steps.signs: Step 2 is the participant's CertEq signature with its host key. The account disclosure carries its author signature. Ed25519, by the author's encryption identity (its signing half, F-14), over digest(hash-input "muster.event.author.v1" {room: the content topic, key: the event key, parents: sorted, author: the author's 64-byte identity hex, value: the event value as dCBOR without authorSig}). actions.name: Export a signature audit trail, and verify it from the file alone
actions.summary: One canonical-CBOR file of everything a proposal's approvals cover, signed by the member who exported it, and verifiable from its bytes alone (exo-403). Exporting writes and sends nothing; handing the file to anyone is the member's own act. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the epoch keys for every event the proposal's history reaches

requirements.name: authorization-key
requirements.target: the keystore's secp256k1 key

steps.does: coordinate_audit(intentId) reduces this member's log to one canonical-CBOR file: the effect and its re-derived materialization; the signing context; the provenance record and the parent-closed lineage it names; every approval with its grade (committed, unattested or rejected) and its signature and attestation events; settlement entries as external reads with the tx hash; and the claims the log alone cannot prove (threshold, stage, disclosure, first epoch). Returns the file as hex, a readable report rendered from it, and its digest.
steps.signs: The exporter's secp256k1 key signs digest(hash-input "muster.signature-audit.v1" {body: the file body as canonical CBOR}).

steps.does: coordinate_verify_audit(hex), or module/tools/muster_audit_verify.nim with no log, keys or network, re-derives the materialization, context, inputs and signing payload from the file; recomputes every content id, the canonical order and the parent closure; checks each approval is signed by the contributor it names and recomputes its grade; and checks the exporter's signature. The first discrepancy is named. Settlement is reported as an external read.
The Markdown report is a pure rendering of the file and carries its digest. It is never authoritative: the file is what verifies.

refusals.what: exporting when the proposal's history reaches an event this member cannot read
refusals.why: refused with that reason, never truncated (invariant 7)

refusals.what: any single change to the file
refusals.why: refused, naming the discrepancy

refusals.what: reporting settlement as verified against the chain
refusals.why: settlement is graded external-read, always

refusals.what: naming a signer who did not approve, or dropping one who did
refusals.why: the file and the report name exactly the contributors the fold recognizes

actions.ui: MusterCard.qml 'Download audit trail' (Room.qml downloadAudit); verifying is headless (coordinate_verify_audit or module/tools/muster_audit_verify.nim)

claims.claim: The file verifies from its bytes alone; any edit is refused with a named reason.
An export never silently drops what the exporter cannot read; it refuses.
Exporting writes nothing and sends nothing.
Settlement in the file is the exporter's report of the chain; a verifier who needs it confirmed must read the chain.
Whoever receives the file reads everything in it; sharing it is the member's choice.

evidence.what: exportAudit / verifyAudit / renderAuditReport
the audit-file spec and its oracles

actions.name: Export a log proof, and verify one
actions.summary: Exports the room's whole raw log as a self-checking slice: every event in canonical order with its content id and the state digest reduce(log) reaches. Verification refuses any single edit. The proof is plaintext and unsigned: it shows the log is internally consistent, not who wrote it. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

steps.does: coordinate_proof() emits {format: muster.log-proof.v1, events: every event of the raw log — forged author-bearing events included — as {parents, key, value} in plaintext, ids: each event's content id, digest: the state digest, epochFrom: 0, epochTo: the current epoch, proofDigest: digest(hash-input "muster.log-proof.v1" {ids, digest, epochFrom, epochTo})}. Nothing is sent.

coordinate_verify_proof(json) recomputes every content id, requires every named parent to be in the proof, requires canonical order, requires the state digest, and requires epochFrom ≤ epochTo. Pure; the first discrepancy is named.

refusals.what: a changed value, key, parent or digest; a dropped middle event; a re-sequenced slice; an inverted epoch range
refusals.why: refused with a named reason

refusals.what: a document that is not a muster.log-proof.v1
refusals.why: it does not parse as a proof

claims.claim: Editing any event of a proof without recomputing it is refused with a named reason.
The same event set gives the same proof, whatever the order or duplication.
An exported proof is plaintext: whoever receives it reads every event in it.
A proof is unsigned and verification checks no signature, so a fully recomputed fabricated proof also verifies. It proves consistency, not origin.

evidence.what: buildProof / verifyProof / toJson

unverified: That a proof is plaintext and that a recomputed fabrication verifies are read from source (proof.nim toJson and verifyProof); no test attempts either. The coordinate_proof description in muster.lidl says nobody outside the epochs can read or forge a proof, which the exported JSON does not bear out.

actions.name: Issue and check a replay-bound authorization
actions.summary: For a proposal the room has folded to executable, issues a grant a host hook can check before it lets a gated module call through (exo-002.7, muster's half). The host half — a broker that refuses a gated call without a matching grant — does not exist yet. Nothing new is agreed: the grant records the room's existing agreement.

requirements.name: authorization-key
requirements.target: the keystore's secp256k1 key

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

steps.does: coordinate_authorization(intentId) issues a grant only if the intent is executable in this member's fold. The grant names the capability (invoke → <module>.<method>; safe → safe.execute; eip191 → eip191.attest; threshold, unanimous, frost → room.attest; otherwise room.<policy>), the materialization root the room agreed on, and a context: the intent's declared context — the same environment (the driver's CAIP-2 environment(), e.g. eip155:31337) and account its approvals were attested under, or room / room for a legacy proposal that declared none — slot = the intent id, expiry = now + 600 s.
steps.signs: secp256k1 recoverable signature by this instance's authorization key over digest(hash-input "muster.authorization.v1" {intentId, capability, materialization, environment, account, slot, expiry})

steps.who: a host hook, or any member
steps.does: coordinate_check_authorization(json) recovers the issuer from the signature and requires slot = intent id and now ≤ expiry. The host must also compare the root with the call it is about to dispatch and the issuer with the issuers its policy trusts; checkAuthorization supports both, but the hosted method passes neither.

refusals.what: a grant for an intent that is not executable
refusals.why: {error: not-executable}; nothing is authorized before agreement

refusals.what: an expired grant, a wrong root, an untrusted issuer, or a tampered capability, slot or issuer
refusals.why: refused with a reason (invariant 2)

claims.claim: A grant exists only for a proposal the room folded to executable.
A grant is worthless for any other root, slot or issuer, or after its expiry.
No host checks grants yet; whether a gated call needs one is up to the host.

evidence.what: the grant, its digest and the pure check
the host-side proposal: gated effects and the hook's four steps

unverified: The not-executable refusal and the context the hosted method fills in are read from source (muster_module.nim).

actions.name: Check whether you are ready to take part in a proposal
actions.summary: The card's 'What this needs': the proposal's five questions plus this instance's readiness, each requirement graded met, missing or unknown with a remedy (exo-002.2). It grades your own keys and configuration only. The module installs nothing. Nothing is agreed.

requirements.name: room-member
requirements.target: the current membership epoch key of the room

disclosure.field: the Safe address the proposal names

steps.who: a member looking at a proposal
steps.does: coordinate_readiness(intentId) reads the proposal's policy and effect from the log, computes its driver's manifest, and grades each requirement for this instance only. module: asks the host whether the module is loaded. environment: probes the configured RPC (eth_chainId) or Bitcoin node (which chain it serves). authority: a Safe's owner set read from the chain (getOwners) and compared locally with your address; a Bitcoin key compared with the account's keys; a roster key with the room's roster. infra: configuration, or a funded LEZ account through lez_core. capability: unknown, since no host broker exists. The payload also carries the manifest (agreement, requirements, the full disclosure with the store node's rows, touches), the profile and the effect.

An account-bound kind (for example safe or eip191) takes kind@<CAIP-10>, or the bare kind when the room holds exactly one account it can use.
